name: Meta Catalog
description: Let your AI check and maintain your Meta product catalogs (Commerce Manager): products with prices, stock and review status, product sets, data feeds and upload errors, and catalog diagnostics. Can update, add or delete products in bulk after confirmation (switched off at install).
instructions:
## Meta Catalog
This connector reads and maintains **Meta product catalogs** (Commerce Manager) through the Graph API (`https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0`): the catalogs of a business portfolio and those shared by clients, products with their review status and errors, product sets, data feeds with their uploads and upload errors, and catalog diagnostics. Writes (batch updates, creating, changing and deleting single products) are installed switched off. Catalogs feed Advantage+ catalog ads, Facebook and Instagram Shops and product tagging, so a change here shows up there.

**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Open https://developers.facebook.com/apps/creation/ and create a business app connected to your business portfolio (or reuse the app of the Meta Ads connector).
2. Recommended, a token that does not expire: in **Business Settings** (https://business.facebook.com/settings) open **Users → System users**, add a system user, then **Assign assets → Catalogs** → your catalog (Manage catalog, or View catalog for read-only). Click **Generate token**, pick the app, choose **Never** as expiry and tick `catalog_management` and `business_management`. Meta can ask you to verify the business portfolio before a system user may generate a token.
3. Quicker alternative for a test: the Graph API Explorer (https://developers.facebook.com/tools/explorer/) with a **User Token** with the same two permissions; it lasts one or two hours unless extended to 60 days in the Access Token Debugger (https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/accesstoken).
4. Paste the token into `META_CATALOG_ACCESS_TOKEN` and the business portfolio id into `META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID` (Business Settings → Business info, or the `business_id=` in the address bar of business.facebook.com). `meta_catalog_list_businesses` lists them for a user token; for a system user token it usually returns an empty list, so take the id from Business Settings.
5. Install, then run `meta_catalog_check_permissions` and `meta_catalog_list_catalogs`.

**Which tool first**: `meta_catalog_list_catalogs` (or `meta_catalog_list_client_catalogs` for catalogs a client shared) gives the `catalog_id`; then `meta_catalog_list_products`, `meta_catalog_list_product_sets`, `meta_catalog_list_feeds` and `meta_catalog_get_diagnostics` take it. For "why are my products rejected or not showing": `meta_catalog_get_diagnostics`, then `meta_catalog_list_products` with `error_priority` HIGH or a `filter` on `review_status`, then `meta_catalog_get_product` (fields `errors`, `review_rejection_reasons`). For feed problems: `meta_catalog_list_feeds` → `meta_catalog_list_feed_uploads` → `meta_catalog_list_upload_errors`.

**Ids**: a product has a Meta `id` (used by `meta_catalog_get_product`, `meta_catalog_update_product`, `meta_catalog_delete_product`) and your own `retailer_id` (the SKU, the `id` column of a feed, used in batch requests and filters). Ids are long numbers: pass them as strings.

**Lists and fields**: lists return `data[]` and `paging.cursors.after`; pass it as `after` for the next page (no `paging.next` means the last page). Each tool returns only the fields in `fields` (each has a useful default). `filter` takes a JSON rule such as `{"retailer_id":{"is_any":["sku1","sku2"]}}`, `{"availability":{"eq":"out of stock"}}` or `{"and":[{"price":{"gt":5000}},{"brand":{"i_contains":"acme"}}]}`; `summary=total_count` adds the number of matching products.

**Money**: when reading, `price` and `sale_price` are strings with the currency (`19.99 EUR`). When creating or updating a single product, `price` is an integer in the minor unit (`1999` = 19.99) with `currency`. In batch requests prices are strings with the currency (`"19.99 EUR"`), and the data uses feed field names (`id` = retailer_id, `title`, `link`, `image_link`).

**Changes reach ads and shops: confirm first.** The write tools are switched off at install; turn them on per tool if the AI should edit the catalog. Before any write, state the catalog, the items (name and retailer_id) and the old and new values, and wait for the user's yes. `meta_catalog_batch_update_items` is asynchronous: follow its handle with `meta_catalog_check_batch_status` until `finished`, then report the errors. Items that a scheduled feed supplies are overwritten by the next feed upload, so for lasting changes fix the feed source (or use a supplementary feed).

**Instagram**: tagging products in posts and publishing are not part of this connector; the Instagram connector covers Instagram publishing, comments and insights.

**Common errors** (in `error.code`)
- 190: the token is invalid or expired; create a new one.
- 10, 200 to 299: a permission is missing (`catalog_management`, `business_management`) or the system user has no access to this catalog. Assign the catalog to the system user and generate the token again.
- 100: a parameter, field or filter is wrong; `error.message` names it. A filter must be valid JSON.
- 4, 17, 613, 80009, 80014: rate limits (80014 is the batch limit); wait a few minutes.

**Out of scope here**: creating or deleting catalogs, feeds and product sets, feed schedules and file uploads, localized catalogs and overrides, pixels and event sources, and catalog ads themselves (see the Meta Ads connector).

META_CATALOG_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Access token
META_CATALOG_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: A system user token from Business Settings → Users → System users → Generate token (expiry Never, permissions catalog_management and business_management), with the catalog assigned to the system user, or a long-lived user token.
META_CATALOG_ACCESS_TOKEN.patternMessage: Meta access tokens start with EA and contain only letters and digits. Paste the token without the word Bearer.

META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID.label: Business portfolio ID
META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID.help: The id of the business portfolio that owns the catalogs: Business Settings → Business info, or business_id= in the address bar of business.facebook.com. meta_catalog_list_businesses lists the businesses of the token.
META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID.patternMessage: The business id is a number of digits only, without act_ or any prefix.

verifyHints.400: Meta refused the request. If the message mentions an access token, the token is invalid or expired (code 190); create a new one.
verifyHints.401: Meta refused the access token. Create a new token (a system user token does not expire) and paste it without the word Bearer.
verifyHints.403: The token lacks a permission (catalog_management, business_management). Generate it again with both permissions.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Meta is rate limiting this app. Wait a few minutes and verify again.

prerequisites: A Meta business portfolio with a product catalog in Commerce Manager, and a Meta app whose system user token (or a long-lived user token) has catalog_management and business_management, with the catalog assigned to that system user. About 10 minutes.

tools.name: meta_catalog_check_permissions
tools.description: List the permissions granted to the access token, each with permission and status (granted or declined). This connector needs catalog_management (read and change catalogs) and business_management (list the business's catalogs). Also a quick check that the token works. Read-only.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_businesses
tools.description: List the business portfolios the token can reach, with id, name and verification_status. Use it to find META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID with a user token; a system user token usually gets an empty list (take the id from Business Settings instead). Needs business_management. The answer has data[] and paging.

fields.description: Comma-separated business fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,verification_status.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_catalogs
tools.description: List the product catalogs owned by the business in META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID, with id, name, product_count, vertical (commerce, hotels, flights, destinations, home_listings, vehicles...) and feed_count. Start here to find a catalog_id. The answer has data[] and paging.cursors.after for the next page.

fields.description: Comma-separated catalog fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,product_count,vertical,feed_count,business,is_catalog_segment,is_local_catalog.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_client_catalogs
tools.description: List the catalogs that other businesses (clients) shared with the business in META_CATALOG_BUSINESS_ID, as an agency or partner sees them, with the roles the business holds on each (permitted_roles). The answer has data[] and paging.

fields.description: Comma-separated catalog fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,product_count,vertical,feed_count,business,is_catalog_segment,is_local_catalog,permitted_roles.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_get_catalog
tools.description: Read one product catalog: name, vertical, product_count, feed_count, owning business and its default and fallback images. Read-only.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

fields.description: Comma-separated catalog fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,product_count,vertical,feed_count,business,is_catalog_segment,is_local_catalog,default_image_url,fallback_image_url.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_products
tools.description: List the products (items) of a catalog with retailer_id, name, price and sale_price (strings with currency, e.g. 19.99 EUR), availability, inventory, review_status (approved, pending, rejected, outdated) and visibility. Filter with a rule such as {"availability":{"eq":"out of stock"}} or {"name":{"i_contains":"shoe"}}, or only items with errors via error_priority. The answer has data[], paging.cursors.after for the next page and, with summary=total_count, summary.total_count.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

fields.description: Comma-separated product fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,retailer_id,name,price,sale_price,currency,availability,inventory,condition,brand,review_status,visibility,url,image_url,retailer_product_group_id.

filter.description: Optional JSON filter rule. Operators: eq, neq, lt, lte, gt, gte, contains, i_contains, not_contains, i_not_contains, starts_with, is_any, is_not_any; combine with {"and": [...]} or {"or": [...]}. Examples: {"retailer_id":{"is_any":["sku1","sku2"]}}, {"review_status":{"eq":"rejected"}}.

error_priority.description: Only items with errors of this priority. HIGH (items that cannot be shown) is the one to fix first.

error_type.description: Optional: only items affected by one issue type, e.g. EMPTY_PRICE, IMAGE_RESOLUTION_LOW, MISSING_CATEGORY, PRICE_OVERRIDE_INVALID (see the products edge reference for the list).

summary.description: Set to total_count to add summary.total_count, the number of matching items.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_get_product
tools.description: Read one catalog product by its Meta id with all details: texts, prices, availability, images, custom labels, GTIN, review_status with review_rejection_reasons, and errors (why it is not shown in ads or shops). Read-only.

product_id.description: The Meta product item id (the id field from meta_catalog_list_products), not the retailer_id.

fields.description: Comma-separated product fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,retailer_id,name,price,sale_price,currency,availability,inventory,condition,brand,review_status,visibility,url,image_url,retailer_product_group_id,description,category,product_type,fb_product_category,additional_image_urls,sale_price_start_date,sale_price_end_date,custom_label_0,custom_label_1,custom_label_2,custom_label_3,custom_label_4,gtin,errors,review_rejection_reasons,product_feed.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_product_sets
tools.description: List the product sets of a catalog (the groups that Advantage+ catalog ads and shop collections use) with id, name, filter rule and product_count. The answer has data[], paging and summary.total_count.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

fields.description: Comma-separated product set fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,filter,product_count,retailer_id.

retailer_id.description: Optional: only the set with this retailer_id.

parent_id.description: Optional: only direct children of this product set; 0 returns the root sets.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_get_product_set
tools.description: Read one product set: name, filter rule, product_count, retailer_id and its collection metadata (latest_metadata, live_metadata with cover image, description and review status). Read-only.

fields.description: Comma-separated product set fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,filter,product_count,retailer_id,latest_metadata,live_metadata.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_product_set_products
tools.description: List the products that belong to a product set, with the same fields and filter as meta_catalog_list_products. The answer has data[] and paging.cursors.after for the next page.

fields.description: Comma-separated product fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,retailer_id,name,price,sale_price,currency,availability,inventory,condition,brand,review_status,visibility,url,image_url,retailer_product_group_id.

filter.description: Optional JSON filter rule, as in meta_catalog_list_products, e.g. {"availability":{"eq":"in stock"}}.

error_priority.description: Only items with errors of this priority. HIGH (items that cannot be shown) is the one to fix first.

summary.description: Set to total_count to add summary.total_count, the number of matching items.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_feeds
tools.description: List the data feeds of a catalog with id, name, product_count, the fetch schedule (url, interval, hour), update_schedule, ingestion_source_type (PRIMARY_FEED or SUPPLEMENTARY_FEED) and latest_upload. The answer has data[] and paging.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

fields.description: Comma-separated feed fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,name,product_count,schedule,update_schedule,latest_upload,ingestion_source_type,file_name,country,default_currency,created_time.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_feed_uploads
tools.description: List the upload sessions of a feed, newest first, with start and end time, how the file came in, items detected, persisted, invalid and deleted, and error and warning counts. Pass an upload id to meta_catalog_list_upload_errors. The answer has data[] and paging.

fields.description: Comma-separated upload fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,start_time,end_time,input_method,url,num_detected_items,num_persisted_items,num_invalid_items,num_deleted_items,error_count,warning_count.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_list_upload_errors
tools.description: List a sample of the errors and warnings of one feed upload: summary, description, severity (fatal: the item was not ingested; warning: a field was dropped) and samples with row_number and retailer_id. The answer has data[], paging and summary.total_count.

error_priority.description: Optional: HIGH for fatal errors only; MEDIUM or LOW for warnings.

fields.description: Comma-separated error fields to return; nested fields use braces, e.g. latest_upload{id,end_time}. Default: id,summary,description,severity,samples.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: meta_catalog_get_diagnostics
tools.description: Get the catalog's diagnostics, the issues Commerce Manager shows: grouped by type with severity (MUST_FIX or OPPORTUNITY), title, number_of_affected_items, details and how to fix them, e.g. missing or invalid attributes, low image quality, policy violations, and Pixel or app issues (EVENT_SOURCE_ISSUES) that hurt Advantage+ catalog ads. The answer has data[] and paging.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

severities.description: Optional JSON array of severities, e.g. ["MUST_FIX"]. Values: MUST_FIX, OPPORTUNITY.

types.description: Optional JSON array of issue types, e.g. ["ATTRIBUTES_MISSING","IMAGE_QUALITY"]. Values: AR_VISIBILITY_ISSUES, ATTRIBUTES_INVALID, ATTRIBUTES_MISSING, CATEGORY, CHECKOUT, DA_VISIBILITY_ISSUES, EVENT_SOURCE_ISSUES, IMAGE_QUALITY, LOW_QUALITY_TITLE_AND_DESCRIPTION, POLICY_VIOLATION, SHOPS_VISIBILITY_ISSUES.

affected_channels.description: Optional JSON array of channels, e.g. ["da","shops","ig_product_tagging"] (da = Advantage+ catalog ads).

affected_entities.description: Optional JSON array: product_item, product_catalog, product_set, product_event.

tools.name: meta_catalog_check_batch_status
tools.description: Check a batch submitted with meta_catalog_batch_update_items: status (finished once processing is done), errors and errors_total_count, warnings and warnings_total_count and, with load_ids_of_invalid_requests true, the ids of the requests that failed. Call it every few seconds until status is finished. Read-only.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

handle.description: The handle returned in handles[] by meta_catalog_batch_update_items.

load_ids_of_invalid_requests.description: true to list the ids of the requests that failed (ids_of_invalid_requests). Default false.

error_priority.description: Optional: only errors of this priority.

tools.name: meta_catalog_batch_update_items
tools.description: Create, update or delete many catalog items in one call (Catalog Batch API, up to 5000 requests, fewer than 3000 recommended). Each request is {"method": "UPDATE", "data": {"id": "<retailer_id>", "price": "19.99 EUR", "availability": "in stock"}}; method CREATE, UPDATE or DELETE, and data uses the feed field names (id = the retailer_id, title, description, link, image_link, price, sale_price, availability, condition, brand), not the names of the single-product tools. The change goes live in ads and shops after processing: state the items and the change and wait for the user's yes. Returns handles[] (check with meta_catalog_check_batch_status) and validation_status with errors per retailer_id.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

requests.description: The requests, each {"method": "CREATE"|"UPDATE"|"DELETE", "data": {"id": "<retailer_id>", ...fields}}. Field names follow the feed spec: title (not name), link (not url), image_link (not image_url). Prices are strings with an ISO currency, e.g. "19.99 EUR"; availability is in stock, out of stock, preorder, available for order or discontinued. DELETE needs only data.id.

item_type.description: Type of the items: PRODUCT_ITEM (default, commerce catalogs) or HOTEL, FLIGHT, DESTINATION, HOME_LISTING, VEHICLE, VEHICLE_OFFER for those verticals.

allow_upsert.description: true (default): an UPDATE for a retailer_id that does not exist creates the item. false: such updates fail instead.

tools.name: meta_catalog_create_product
tools.description: Add one product to a catalog. Required: retailer_id (your SKU), name, price (an integer in the currency's minor unit, 1999 = 19.99), currency, image_url; add description, url, availability, brand, condition and sale_price as needed. An existing retailer_id is updated instead (allow_upsert). The product can appear in ads and shops after review: confirm the data with the user first. Returns the new product id.

catalog_id.description: Catalog id (a long number, as a string) from meta_catalog_list_catalogs.

retailer_id.description: Your unique id for the item (SKU); the id column of a feed.

price.description: Price as an integer in the currency's minor unit (cents): 1999 = 19.99.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR or USD.

sale_price.description: Optional sale price in the minor unit, like price.

image_url.description: Public URL of the main product image.

retailer_product_group_id.description: Optional group id that links variants (sizes, colours) of one product.

tools.name: meta_catalog_update_product
tools.description: Change fields of one catalog product by its Meta id: price, sale_price, availability, inventory, name, description, image, link or visibility. Only the fields you pass change. A product that a feed also supplies is overwritten again at the next feed upload. State the product and the old and new values and wait for the user's yes. Returns {"success": true}.

product_id.description: The Meta product item id (the id field from meta_catalog_list_products), not the retailer_id.

price.description: New price in the currency's minor unit: 1999 = 19.99.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code, when the price changes currency.

sale_price.description: New sale price in the minor unit.

visibility.description: published shows the item; staging hides it from ads and shops.

tools.name: meta_catalog_delete_product
tools.description: Delete one product from its catalog by Meta id. Ads and shop listings that show it stop showing it, and it cannot be restored (add it again to recreate it). A feed that still lists the item adds it back at its next upload. Confirm the product (name, retailer_id) with the user first. Returns {"success": true}.

product_id.description: The Meta product item id (the id field from meta_catalog_list_products), not the retailer_id.
